# clausona

> clausona is a free, open-source CLI and terminal dashboard for running multiple Claude Code and OpenAI Codex CLI accounts on one machine. Each account keeps its own sign-in in its own config directory (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or CODEX_HOME). Skills, hooks, plugins, settings and global instructions are shared between the accounts of each tool, and conversation history can be shared too, so a conversation started under one account can be resumed under another. It also shows every account's 5-hour and weekly plan usage side by side. It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows, has no proxy or daemon, and is not affiliated with Anthropic or OpenAI.

Facts:

- Install: `curl -fsSL https://github.com/larcane97/clausona/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash` (macOS, Linux) or `irm https://github.com/larcane97/clausona/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows PowerShell). Needs Node.js 20 or later.
- Set up: `clausona init` registers the accounts already signed in; `clausona add claude:work` or `clausona add codex:work` adds one; `csn use work` switches; `clausona run claude:personal` runs one session under another account.
- Shared history: `clausona config <profile> --merge-sessions`; then `claude --resume` and `claude --continue`, and on macOS and Linux `codex resume`, see conversations from every account that shares history.
- Never shared: sign-ins, Claude Code's `.claude.json` (including `claude mcp add` servers) and the state it keeps for one account or org (policy limits, remote managed settings, the MCP sign-in cache, the background daemon with its scheduled tasks and Remote Control folders, which a profile sets up on its own), and Codex's auth.json, app-server daemon, memories and its databases other than the thread store (which merged sessions share on macOS and Linux).
- Lightweight: a shell hook and symbolic links, with no app, daemon or proxy. A plain `claude` or `codex` launch reads a cached script in the shell and skips clausona; on an M4 Pro Mac, `claude --version` took a median 25 ms with the hook and 25 ms without it. clausona's own process (about 0.3 s) runs on the first launch after a change such as `csn use`, on every launch of an API profile, and on every `clausona run`, routed or not.
- A running session never moves to another account. `clausona use` and `clausona run <profile>` run on the account the user names, and a route picks one only when a run starts. Keep the accounts to what they're for, such as work and personal use, within Anthropic's and OpenAI's terms.
- Dynamic routing: `clausona route add main` makes a route of every Claude Code account (`--tool codex` for Codex). `clausona run --route main` starts on one of them that still has plan quota left, and says on stderr which one. After `clausona route dir <dir> <route>` or `clausona route default <route>`, plain `clausona run claude` or `clausona run codex` takes a route too. See [dynamic routing in the Claude Code guide](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/multiple-claude-code-accounts/#routing) and [Routing](https://github.com/larcane97/clausona/blob/main/docs/routing.md).
- Extensions: `clausona skills`, `clausona mcp`, `clausona hooks` and the dashboard's Extensions screen list the skills, MCP servers and hooks that each Claude Code and Codex account loads in a project. An item can be turned off or deleted, after a confirm step and behind a backup, and `undo` puts the last change back. See [the Extensions guide](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/claude-code-skills-mcp-hooks/) and [Extensions](https://github.com/larcane97/clausona/blob/main/docs/extensions.md).

## Guides

- [How to use multiple Claude Code accounts on one machine](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/multiple-claude-code-accounts/): CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR by hand, what must not be shared, and the clausona way, including shared conversation history, and dynamic routing, which picks the account each `clausona run` starts on.
- [How to use multiple Codex CLI accounts on one machine](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/multiple-codex-cli-accounts/): one CODEX_HOME per account, which files to share, and which must stay with each account, and dynamic routing for Codex accounts.
- [Run parallel Claude Code agents on different accounts and models](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/parallel-claude-code-agents/): subagents run out of sight and all spend one account. Instead, run each agent as a separate Claude Code session with `clausona run <profile>` in any runner (a terminal, tmux, herdr, Orca or Superset), on an account or an API model such as DeepSeek. The superset-fleet, herdr-fleet, orca-fleet and tmux-fleet plugins add a coordinator in each runner: one Claude Code or Codex session plans, routes by rules and usage, checks and retires workers. Install only the one for your runner.
- [Claude Code와 Codex 계정 여러 개를 동시에 쓰는 법](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/ko/): the same guide in Korean.
- [Run parallel Claude Code and Codex agents in herdr](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/parallel-agents-in-herdr/): the herdr-fleet plugin. One session in a herdr pane creates a worktree per task with `herdr worktree create`, starts `clausona run <profile>` in each pane, waits with `herdr agent prompt --wait`, checks the pushed branch and, once you approve, removes the worktree without force.
- [Run parallel Claude Code and Codex agents in Orca](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/parallel-agents-in-orca/): the orca-fleet plugin. One session creates an Orca worktree per task, starts `clausona run <profile>` in its terminal (overriding the CODEX_HOME Orca sets), waits with `orca terminal wait --for tui-idle`, checks the pushed branch and, once you approve, removes the worktree, which also deletes its local branch.
- [Run parallel Claude Code and Codex agents in tmux](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/parallel-agents-in-tmux/): the tmux-fleet plugin, for plain tmux 3.2 or newer on macOS, Linux or WSL, with no GUI, so it also works over SSH. One session in a tmux pane adds a git worktree per task on branch `fleet/<task>`, opens a tmux window labelled with the task and profile, and types `clausona run <profile>` into it. Each worker reports its state: a Claude Code worker through hooks passed with `--settings` from a file in its worktree, a Codex worker by ringing the terminal bell, which a tmux hook records. The session waits on those events, checks the pushed branch and, once you approve, removes the worktree with `git worktree remove` without force and closes the window.
- [See which skills, MCP servers and hooks Claude Code loads, and turn them off](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/guides/claude-code-skills-mcp-hooks/): the skills, MCP servers and hooks Claude Code and Codex load in a project, for each account, on the dashboard's Extensions screen or with `clausona skills`, `clausona mcp` and `clausona hooks`. How to turn one off in one project or everywhere, delete it behind a backup, and undo the change.
- [Claude Code 에이전트를 여러 계정과 모델로 병렬 실행하기](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/ko/parallel-agents/): the parallel agents guide in Korean.
- [herdr에서 Claude Code와 Codex 에이전트를 계정별로 병렬 실행하기](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/ko/parallel-agents-in-herdr/): the herdr guide in Korean.
- [Orca에서 Claude Code와 Codex 에이전트를 계정별로 병렬 실행하기](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/ko/parallel-agents-in-orca/): the Orca guide in Korean.
- [tmux에서 Claude Code와 Codex 에이전트를 계정별로 병렬 실행하기](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/ko/parallel-agents-in-tmux/): the tmux guide in Korean.
- [Claude Code와 Codex가 불러오는 스킬, MCP 서버, hook 확인하고 끄기](https://larcane97.github.io/clausona/ko/skills-mcp-hooks/): the Extensions guide in Korean.
